newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAGACH LOSES WORLD GOLD MEDAL AND $60,000.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAGACH LOSES WORLD GOLD MEDAL AND $60,000.

text.p: Ukraine's world shot put champion Aleksandr Bagach has been stripped of his gold medal after failing a drug test, the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) said on Thursday.
In a statement, the IAAF said the Olympic bronze medallist had tested positive for the stimulant ephedrine and would lose his gold medal and the $60,000 winner's prize.
The IAAF said French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan had also tested positive for ephedrine.
"Following the recent decision by the IAAF congress, these athletes will be issued a public warning and disqualified from the competition," the statement said.
"The results they achieved at these world championships have been cancelled."

American John Godina, who received a wild card entry as defending champion, will now take the shot gold medal, German Oliver-Sven Buder the silver and another American, C.J. Hunter, fiancee of new world 100 metres champion Marion Jones, has been awarded the bronze.
It is the second time that Bagach has been caught cheating with banned substances during his career.
The Ukrainian was banned for two years in 1989 after he was found to have excessive levels of the male hormone testosterone in his body when he was competing for the former Soviet Union.

Bagach, 30, would have been banned for life if he had tested positive for a serious drug such as steroids but he will escape with a warning after the new rule introduced by the IAAF before the championships.

The 30-year-old Bagach equalled his personal best by recording 21.47 metres at his third attempt to win the competition in Athens on Saturday. He said afterwards that he could not believe his performance.

The Ukrainian struggled to make his way back to the top after being banned for two years for testosterone following third place in the 1989 European Cup in Gateshead, England. As a result, the Soviet team lost their place in the World Cup.
Bagach, however, could clearly not resist the temptation to cheat his way to glory with banned substances again.
Under previous rules athletes caught using stimulants would be banned for three months but the IAAF's congress decided to soften the ban to a public warning at their meeting before the championships.
